record.original_question: Let φ be a transitive pseudo-Anosov flow on a closed, oriented 3-manifold, and let γ1 , . . . , γk be a collection of closed orbits. Let Z ⊆ Rk be the closure of the set of multislopes such that simultaneous Dehn surgery on the γi ’s results in a pseudo-Anosov flow admitting a transverse codimension 1 foliation. What structure does the set Z have?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed, oriented $3$-manifold and let $\varphi$ be a transitive pseudo-Anosov flow on $M$ (i.e., a topological pseudo-Anosov flow that has a dense orbit). Fix a finite collection $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k$ of closed orbits of $\varphi$. For each such closed orbit $\gamma_i$, removing a tubular neighborhood produces a torus boundary component, and one may perform Dehn filling along $\gamma_i$ with a slope $s_i \in \mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ (a "multislope" being a tuple $(s_1,\dots,s_k)$). For each multislope $s=(s_1,\dots,s_k) \in \mathbb{R}^k$ for which the resulting Dehn–Goodman–Fried-type surgery is defined, the surgered manifold inherits a (pseudo-)Anosov flow $\varphi_s$.

Define
$$Z \;=\; \overline{\bigl\{\, s \in \mathbb{R}^k \;:\; \varphi_s \text{ is a pseudo-Anosov flow admitting a transverse codimension-one foliation}\,\bigr\}} \;\subseteq\; \mathbb{R}^k,$$
where the closure is taken in $\mathbb{R}^k$ with the standard topology.

Determine the structure of the set $Z$. (For example: is $Z$ always a finite union of convex polyhedra, a semi-algebraic set, a union of products of intervals, or some other geometrically describable object? Give a complete description of the possible shapes of $Z$ in terms of data associated to $\varphi$ and the orbits $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the global shape of the set of multislopes yielding pseudo-Anosov flows with a transverse codimension-one foliation after Dehn surgery on closed orbits. Recent work (e.g., on veering triangulations and transverse foliations, 2024–2025) gives partial results, such as one-parameter examples where the set of slopes admitting a transverse foliation is an interval (e.g., for the knot $10_{145}$, transverse foliations exist for $s \in (-\infty,3)$ but not for $s \in [5,\infty)$). However, no general structural description of $Z$ in higher dimensions appears in the literature, and the problem is posed as a question without a known answer.

status_evidence.title: Veering triangulations and transverse foliations
status_evidence.snippet: Every codimension-1 foliation transverse to a transitive pseudo-Anosov flow is carried by a single branched surface; partial results on slope intervals admitting transverse foliations after surgery.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work gives partial, low-dimensional results but no general structural description of the closure Z.

status_evidence.title: Pseudo-Anosov flows on hyperbolic L-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) investigations of transverse foliations to surgered pseudo-Anosov flows; demonstrates ongoing active research.
status_evidence.claim: The structural problem remains an active open research direction.
